**Theorem.** The Lindenbaum algebra generated by an infinite set $P$ of proposit
ional variables is atomless.

**Proof.**

Let $B$ denote the Lindenbaum algebra, i.e., the Boolean algebra of equivalence
classes $[\varphi]$ of propositional formulas (built from $P$) modulo logical eq
uivalence. This is the free Boolean algebra on the generating set $P$. Its zero
element is $[\bot]$ (the class of contradictions) and its unit is $[\top]$.

Recall that an **atom** of a Boolean algebra is a nonzero element $a$ such that
there is no element $b$ with $0 < b < a$.

**Key observation.** Every formula $\varphi$ mentions only finitely many proposi
tional variables. Let $\operatorname{Vars}(\varphi) \subseteq P$ denote this fin
ite set.

We claim every nonzero element of $B$ fails to be an atom.

Let $[\varphi] \in B$ be nonzero, i.e., $\varphi$ is satisfiable. Then $\operato
rname{Vars}(\varphi) = \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$ is finite. Since $P$ is infinite, th
ere exists a variable $q \in P \setminus \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$.

Consider the element $[\varphi \wedge q] \in B$.

- **$[\varphi \wedge q] \neq 0$:** Since $\varphi$ is satisfiable, there is a tr
uth assignment to $p_1, \dots, p_n$ making $\varphi$ true. Extend this assignmen
t by setting $q = \text{true}$. This satisfies $\varphi \wedge q$, so $\varphi \
wedge q$ is not a contradiction.

- **$[\varphi \wedge q] < [\varphi]$, i.e., $[\varphi \wedge q] \neq [\varphi]$:
** We need $\varphi \not\equiv \varphi \wedge q$, equivalently $\varphi \wedge \
neg q$ is satisfiable. Since $q \notin \operatorname{Vars}(\varphi)$, the truth
value of $\varphi$ is independent of $q$. Take any satisfying assignment of $\va
rphi$ (on $p_1, \dots, p_n$) and set $q = \text{false}$. This satisfies $\varphi
 \wedge \neg q$, so $\varphi \not\equiv \varphi \wedge q$.

Therefore $0 < [\varphi \wedge q] < [\varphi]$, which shows $[\varphi]$ is **not
** an atom.

Since $[\varphi]$ was an arbitrary nonzero element of $B$, no nonzero element is
 an atom. Hence $B$ is **atomless**. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
